title: Stop At Usage Limit
bottom_line: End a prompt with until /session-token-utilization gets to 90% and the agent stops there, at once or after a wrap-up.

sections.heading: Add the limit phrase to a prompt, or type /token-utilization

blocks.title: What to type
blocks.code:
Do XXX until /session-token-utilization gets to 90%
Do YYY until /weekly-token-utilization gets to 70%
/token-utilization [off]
blocks.caption: The first two lines set a limit for the task the prompt starts. The third shows the current limit, or removes it with off.

blocks.title: The ways to use it
rows: `... until /session-token-utilization gets to 90%`
Stop when the session (5-hour) window reaches 90%.
`... until /weekly-token-utilization gets to 70%`
Stop when the weekly window reaches 70%.
both, joined by `or` / `and`
Stop at whichever is reached first. One mode covers both.
the phrase in a slash command's arguments
The same, for example `/plan-tools:plan-implement-complete plan.md until /session-token-utilization gets to 80%`.
`/token-utilization`
Show the limit, its current reading, the mode and the state.
`/token-utilization off`
Remove the limit.

blocks.text: The phrase, from "until" through the percentage, is removed before the model or the command reads the prompt.
The limit lasts until it is reached, until a new prompt names another limit, or until `/token-utilization off`. Follow-up prompts you type keep it.

sections.heading: You need a mod-loading Claude Code and a claude.ai subscription

cards.title: Claude Code that loads mods
cards.text: The plugin registers a TypeScript module through `hooks/hooks.json`, not a skill, so your Claude Code version must load plugin mods.

cards.title: A claude.ai subscription
cards.text: With it, Claude Code reports the session (5-hour) and weekly usage windows, which the mod needs.

blocks.title: Nothing to configure
items: State is kept in the plugin's own store and survives a reload.

sections.heading: Choose stop immediately or wrap up first

blocks.text: When you send a prompt that names a limit, a question asks what should happen at the limit.

cards.title: Stop immediately
cards.text: The running turn is cancelled and every running subagent is stopped.

cards.title: Wrap up first
cards.text: The agent may finish a small remaining piece or record where it stands, then stops. Running subagents get the same wrap-up message.

points.text: Usage is cut off 5 points above the limit, at most 100%.

blocks.title: The prompt is not sent, with the reason shown, when
items: the percentage is missing or outside 1 to 100;
the window is already at or past the limit;
the mode question is closed with Esc;
the prompt comes from `claude -p`, where nobody can answer the question.

steps.title: The limit is reached
steps.text: One transcript line marks the moment and gives the handoff path.

steps.title: The agent wraps up
steps.text: It finishes a small remainder or stops, and ends with handoff notes: what is done, what is in progress, what is left, and the next step.

steps.title: The notes are saved
steps.text: The mod saves the main agent's final wrap-up message as `.claude/handoffs/HANDOFF-<first 8 characters of the session id>.md` under the project root.

steps.title: You resume later
steps.text: Ask the agent to read that file first.

blocks.title: About the file
items: Each session writes its own file, so parallel sessions never overwrite each other's notes.
The mod also writes `.claude/handoffs/.gitignore` containing `*`, so the folder stays out of git.

sections.heading: After the stop, automatic prompts ask before they run

blocks.text: A prompt you type runs normally and clears the stop. Something else may try to restart the agent: a background task's notification, a scheduled task, `/loop`, or auto-resume's `continue`. Then the mod sends a notification through Claude Code's own notification channel (your `preferredNotifChannel` setting) and asks whether to run it.

blocks.title: Your answer
rows: Yes, run it
It runs, and later automatic prompts run without asking.
No, or Esc
It is dropped, and the next one asks again.

sections.heading: Check the status line or type /token-utilization

blocks.title: Two places to look
rows: The status line, while a limit is set
For example `stop at session 90% (now 62%), wrap-up`
The reply to `/token-utilization`
The limit, its current reading, the mode and the state

sections.heading: The stop can land a point or two above your number

cards.title: Readings move in whole points
cards.text: Usage readings arrive with model responses, so the stop can land a point or two above the number you named.

cards.title: First prompt of a session
cards.text: A new session has no reading until its first response, so a limit that is already passed is not caught when the prompt is sent.

points.text: The limit is set, and the first reading stops the agent.

cards.title: No reading at all
cards.text: Without a usage reading (for example, no subscription), the status line says `no reading yet`, and a transcript line warns after the first turn that the limit cannot take effect.

cards.title: The session must be open
cards.text: The mod can only act on an open session. Background shell commands keep running; they spend no tokens.

next_action.text: End your next long prompt with `until /session-token-utilization gets to 90%`.
next_action.detail: Pick Wrap up first to get handoff notes in `.claude/handoffs/`.
